T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based approach with frameworks like React or Angular to design an intuitive and responsive interface for the problem library.
T1.notes: Focus on user experience and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem library operations such as adding, updating, deleting, and retrieving problems.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema with tables for problems, categories, and tags. Use normalization to avoid redundancy.
T3.notes: Optimize for query performance and scalability.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a feature to allow users to submit code, store submissions, and track their status.
T4.notes: Implement security measures to prevent malicious code submissions.

T5.implementation_approach: Use a sandbox environment to execute user-submitted code and compare outputs against test cases.
T5.notes: Ensure isolation and resource limits for code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface for user profiles, displaying progress, achievements, and settings.
T6.notes: Include visual elements like charts for progress tracking.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profile data, including updates to progress and achievements.
T7.notes: Ensure secure handling of sensitive user information.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a database schema for user profiles, including tables for user details, progress, and achievements.

T9.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface that displays top users based on their scores and achievements.
T9.notes: Include sorting and filtering options for better usability.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user scores and achievements.
T10.notes: Ensure real-time updates for leaderboard rankings.

T11.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and explanations for problems in an organized and accessible manner.
T11.notes: Allow users to toggle visibility of hints.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and explanations, including adding, updating, and retrieving them.
data_structures: Relational tables for hints and explanations
T12.notes: Ensure proper categorization and tagging for easy retrieval.

T13.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the problem library.
T13.notes: Focus on edge cases and performance testing.

T14.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation feature using various test cases and scenarios.
T14.notes: Include tests for security and resource limits.

T15.implementation_approach: Test user profile features, including progress tracking and achievement updates.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the leaderboard functionality, including sorting, filtering, and real-time updates.
T16.notes: Verify scalability and performance under high load.

T17.implementation_approach: Test the hints and explanations feature for proper retrieval and display.
T17.notes: Ensure hints are displayed correctly and are accessible.

T18.implementation_approach: Deploy the ACM problem-solving platform using containerization and cloud services.
T18.notes: Ensure scalability, security, and monitoring post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem(id={self.id}, title='{self.title}', difficulty='{self.difficulty}')>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'
    
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now(), nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)

    user = db.relationship('User', back_populates='solutions')
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', back_populates='solutions')

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} language={self.language} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id}>"

# app/routes.py
# Layer: assembly
# Purpose: Aggregate all blueprints

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Configure the application
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

    return app

from app import create_app

app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles and Progress Tracking: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays a leaderboard to encourage competition among users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn and improve.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
